introduction: Today, within the Octave of Christmas, we celebrate the Holy Family of Jesus, Mary and Joseph. Sirach teaches children to honor their parents and care for them in old age. Paul describes the virtues of a Christian home: compassion, kindness, forgiveness and love. In the Gospel, Joseph protects Mary and the child by fleeing to Egypt, and later brings them home to Nazareth. Let us pray for our families.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, let the peace of Christ rule in our hearts. Let us bring our families to the Lord in prayer.
intentions: For the Church, the family of God: that she may be a home of compassion and forgiveness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families: that they may live with kindness, patience and love, after the example of the Holy Family. Let us pray to the Lord.
For refugees and migrant families, like the Holy Family in Egypt: that they may find safety and welcome. Let us pray to the Lord.
For elderly parents and grandparents: that they may be honored and cared for by their children. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families in difficulty, divided or grieving: that the Lord may bring them healing and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you gave us the Holy Family as a model of love. Help our families to grow in kindness and forgiveness, and bring us all to your eternal home. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Flight into Egypt
reflection.body:
The feast of the Holy Family reminds us that God chose to enter the world through a family, with all its joys and dangers.

Sirach gives very practical advice about family life. "He who honors his father will make atonement for sins." He speaks of caring for parents as they grow old: "My son, help your father in his old age, and don't grieve him as long as he lives. If he fails in understanding, have patience with him." This patience is a holy duty.

Paul describes the clothing of a Christian household: "Put on therefore, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance; bearing with one another, and forgiving each other." And above all, love: "Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection." He adds, "let the peace of God rule in your hearts." Paul's advice to husbands, wives and children belongs to his time, but its heart is this: mutual love and care, in the Lord.

In the Gospel, the Holy Family is in danger. An angel warns Joseph in a dream: "Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt." King Herod wants to kill the child. So Joseph takes them by night and they become refugees in a foreign land. Later, when Herod has died, the angel tells Joseph to return, and they settle in Nazareth.

The Holy Family knew fear, exile and uncertainty. They show us that holiness is not the absence of difficulties but faithfulness and love in the middle of them. Joseph, again, listens and acts to protect those entrusted to him.

Today, pray for your family by name. Think of one virtue from Paul's list that your home most needs, and practice it this week. And remember families who are refugees today, as the Holy Family once was.
